asr_contract.source: B-04 gate, measured 2026-09-10 against AssemblyAI batch API
asr_contract.rule_1_send_whole_phrase: Send the ENTIRE sung phrase to AssemblyAI as ONE continuous audio blob. Measured: continuous legato phrase = 100% syllable accuracy; the same syllables chopped into per-note files with silence between = 25%. Isolation destroys recognition.
asr_contract.rule_2_never_pad: Do not insert silence between notes before upload. Do not upload per-note segments. Ever.
asr_contract.rule_5_division_of_labour: Pitch DSP (local, in-browser) owns per-note pitch and timing accuracy. AssemblyAI owns the syllable SEQUENCE over the whole phrase. Do not ask AAI which note was flat; do not ask the DSP which syllable was sung.
asr_contract.rule_6_word_boost: Always send word_boost with boost_param 'high'. Measured: on degraded audio it moved 0% to 62.5%. On clean audio it is a no-op, so it is free insurance.
asr_contract.rule_7_normalise_before_compare: Always run the transcript through homophone_map before scoring. AAI returned canonical solfege spellings on clean audio, but the map costs nothing and catches 'soul/so', 'ray', 'tea/si'.
asr_contract.confidence: VERIFIED on synthetic (espeak+ffmpeg) audio. NOT yet verified on a human voice. Human vowels sustain longer and consonants are weaker, so treat the 100% as an upper bound. One real human clip must confirm before the demo is recorded.

default_keys.note: Pick the key from the learner's measured comfortable range at onboarding. Never force a fixed key; a learner straining an octave too high will score badly for reasons that have nothing to do with their ear.

tolerance_cents.note: Beginners are wide. 50 cents is a quarter tone; below that a human hears 'the right note, slightly off'. Do not punish inside 15 cents - that is measurement noise on a phone mic.
